DynamoDB adds native vector indexing and filtered similarity search beside operational records, removing a separate replication pipeline. AWS claims recall above 99%; the announcement does not provide a full comparative benchmark.

EG-GRPO: Evidence-Guided Step-level Credit Assignment for Deep Search Agents
Sijia Luo, Mengjie Gao, Yuxiao He, Mengshu Sun, Cuiping Li, Hong Chen, Jing Zhang
EG-GRPO rewards the first search step that finds support for a required claim, then compares actions from similar evidence states. The 4B agent reaches 45.9% accuracy on GAIA.
ClueFlow: Learning Long-Horizon Search through Attributed Research-State Transitions
Yicheng Wang, Wentao Tan, Yidan Huang, Yifei Liu, Qiong Cao

ClueFlow links browser actions to research-state updates and the final answer. It uses those attribution chains for supervised learning and turn-level RL. In a controlled comparison, selected supervision matches all-turn SFT with about 30% of its training tokens.
Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning
Kyuyoung Kim, Zilin Xiao, Zhiyuan Wang, Avinash Atreya, Ke Yang, Jinwoo Shin, Kecheng Hao

Retrieval Program Learning trains a model to compose executable search programs and learn from constrained mutations of unsuccessful programs. Its 4B model averages 51.5% exact-match accuracy across seven QA benchmarks.
HybridResearcher: Bridging the Structured-Unstructured Boundary for Deep Research Agents
Soyoung Yoon, Peiran Xu, Han Wang, Ruofan Wu, Xiaodong Yu, Feng Yan, Mohit Bansal, Debiao Li, Seung…

HybridResearcher trains a 4B agent to connect database results with unstructured evidence. It constructs bridge trajectories around entities from validated single-source tasks and rejects examples solvable from either side alone. It improves pass@8 over its base model by 30.0 percentage points.
OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
Yu Zhou, Cheng-Fu Yang, Rui Sun, Di Wu, Sibo Peng, Mingyang Zhang, Zhen Yang, Ruiyi Zhang, Nanyun P…

OpenVLHarness combines consistent tool interfaces with persistent, addressable multimodal evidence. Programs can reuse images, structured data, and web sources across steps. It improves average scores by 9.7–12.6 points over matched no-tool baselines.
The Scheduler Is a Hidden Retriever: How Asynchrony Shapes Evidence Acquisition in Search Agents
Ruiyang Ren, Yuhao Wang, Yinan Zhang, Chunyan Miao

This study shows that asynchronous result timing changes what search agents retrieve next. Confluent Evidence Acquisition waits for each subquestion’s evidence and allocates shared search independently of arrival order, improving accuracy over early commitment by up to 12.6 percentage points.
Fine-tune a search agent with multi-turn RL on Amazon SageMaker AI
Huibin Shen, Pooja Karadgi, Sifei Li, Lorenzo Stella

AWS fine-tunes a search agent to choose between lexical and vector search, rewarding nDCG@10 and penalizing turn or token overruns. On BrowseComp-Plus, nDCG@10 improves by 23.7% relative to the base model.
Zhiyu Li, Zeyu Zhang, Linyun Liu, Yiwei Bu, Chenyang Xi

MemT-1.0 integrates updatable memory into model computation and expands capacity through Mixture-of-Storage. At a 128K-token history length, the Nano model delivers about 1.86× end-to-end inference speedup over a full-context KV-cache baseline.
AdaExploreBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Proactive Exploration and Test-time Adaptation in Evolving Environments
Rui Wang, Zishen Lai, Jiayu Liu, Cheng Qian, Jeonghwan Kim

AdaExploreBench hides environment rules and changes them without announcement, testing whether agents gather evidence and reconsider stale assumptions. Across eight evaluated models, GPT-6 Sol achieves 61.9% calibrated accuracy.
Chinese Decision: A Family of Language Models for Single-Pass Probabilistic Decision-Making
Qiang Yan (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences)

Some applications need candidate probabilities rather than generated explanations. Chinese Decision normalizes candidate-letter logits from a single forward pass for Boolean, categorical, and ordinal decisions. Its completed 0.8B model reaches 72.24% general-domain accuracy on CJ-Bench.
The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do

A single agent mixed up rules when onboarding data columns across recommendation pipelines. Meta moved routing and reliability checks into a thin orchestrator and isolated domain reasoning in specialist agents. Configuration preparation fell from three to four days manually to under an hour.
HEM-Med: A Hierarchical Agentic Memory Framework for Safe Multi-Center Medication Recommendation
Min Xiao, Jin Li, Shoujin Wang, Yeguang Zhen, Yishuo Li, Wenpeng Lu

Separate shared experience from local prescribing patterns before generating a medication set. HEM-Med retrieves both memory levels and enforces safety and formulary constraints during decoding. It reports an F1 score of 0.4532 on the multicenter eICU dataset.
Humanity's Last Choice: A Common Evaluation Standard for Generative Engine Optimization
Qianfeng Wen, Yifan Simon Liu, Difan Jiao, Junda Wu, Di Bai, Jintao Liu, Xidong Wu, Zhenwei Tang

Generative-search optimization studies often allow different source edits, making their results difficult to compare. This position paper organizes edits by layer, action, and target signal, then specifies controlled comparisons. It proposes a protocol rather than reporting a benchmark performance gain.

Text revision often regenerates large amounts of unchanged context. Causal Edit Serialization emits pointer-addressed edit programs inside a causal token stream while retaining the original context. The localization components add approximately 0.34–0.41% parameters at the tested depths.
LED: Improving Masked Diffusion Language Models by Lookahead Editing
Yuyan Zhou, Zeyuan Yang, Yuxuan Song, Zhicheng Cai, Hongli Yu, Weiying Ma, Hao Zhou, James Kwok

Masked diffusion commits tokens too early to revise poor choices. LED keeps an editable proposal state and refines future predictions before committing them. Its 7B model improves the eight-benchmark average by 11.4 points over standard masked-diffusion supervised fine-tuning.
On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
Eliezer Shlomi, Eliron Rahimi, Avi Mendelson, Chaim Baskin

Diffusion decoding must predict both tokens and the order in which positions are committed. SPOT learns that order, proposes a tree of continuations, and verifies branches in parallel. Reported peak throughput is 3.2 times standard decoding.
Trust but Verify: Designing Region-Inhomogeneous Forward Dynamics for Discrete Diffusion

Observed context can be wrong even when a diffusion model treats it as fixed. Region-dependent corruption teaches the model to detect and revise suspicious context. With 20% uniform-random corruption, infilling token F1 improves by 6.4 points.
Prism Attention: Proposal-Refined Index Sharing Mechanism for Efficient LLMs Inference
Zhenxu Tian, Kebin Liu, Zhengwu Yang, Yi Su, Qingqing Dang, Yanlin Sha, Kaipeng Deng, Dianhai Yu, Y…

Sparse attention can spend much of its savings recomputing token indices across layers. Prism Attention shares coarse proposals and refines them locally for each layer. It reports 3.4-times end-to-end decoding speedup over FlashAttention at a 128K context length.
Accelerating Mamba-2 with High-Performance Forward Pass Kernels in NVIDIA CUDA Tile

Mamba-2 can lose time moving intermediate state between kernels. The authors use cuTile to fuse tiled computation and optimize memory layouts for the forward pass. On B300, the kernels run 1.14–1.82 times faster than the Triton reference.
LSNR: Learned Sparse News Recommendations with Attentive User Modeling
David Vos, Andrew Yates, Maarten de Rijke
Encode articles separately, then learn which ones matter. LSNR combines weighted sparse article vectors with a user-level semantic expansion, improving MIND NDCG@10 by about 11% over STAR.
Predictable Scaling: Efficient Model Exploration via Scaling-Law Prediction
Aishwarya Wesanekar, Sheng-Tao Yang, Jiawei Zhang, Flavio Sales Truzzi, Chen Chen, Nader Beigiparas…

Predictable Scaling evaluates ranking-model changes with reduced-scale proxies and estimates their full-scale effects using historical learning curves. Training compute falls by 88% and 79% on two industrial ranking models.
GenRecs Tokenization: Transforming Ads Recommendation at Meta with Stable Model Vocabulary

Meta represents ads with a stable semantic vocabulary that combines content and engagement signals. Integrated with its ads models, tokenization is associated with a reported 0.35% conversion lift, measured internally in February 2026.
Learning User Representations to Improve Simulation Fidelity
Shuhaib Mehri, Philippe Laban, Michel Galley, Dilek T\"ur, Jennifer Neville, Jianfeng Gao

UserRepGen learns user descriptions from feedback on reconstructed conversations. Evaluation covers 700 conversations and examines transfer to unseen tasks and population diversity, tying profile quality to the behavior a profile induces.
Reasoning Reranking with Semantic IDs as the Sole Item Representation
Zhenwei Tang, Jintao Liu, Di Bai, Xidong Wu, Xinwu Cheng

ReRankID tests rerankers that see only compact semantic item IDs. Untuned models often copy input order. Ranking-reward training approaches strong text-reading baselines whose prompts are about 20 times longer.
Learning Personalized Memory Gating from Delayed One-Sided Feedback
Kaixuan Ji, Zixiang Chen, Wenting Zhao, Cheng Qian, Heng Wang, Weizhi Zhang, Jielin Qiu, Liangwei Y…

A shared memory-retention policy misses user-specific reuse patterns. This work combines an offline prior with online exploration and delayed feedback. On PerMemBench-S at budget 500, the micro-average coverage score reaches 84.48.
VISTA: Steering LLMs with Latent User Values Inferred from a Few Survey Answers
Yinuo Xu, Jadie Adams, Brian Hu, Shivani Kumar, David Jurgens, Arslan Basharat

VISTA infers latent values from a small set of survey answers and steers a frozen language model. On the World Values Survey, it retains 94% of the full-history gain after asking only 6% of the questionnaire.
Chance-Constrained Personalized LLM Routing with Online Preference Learning
Ameya Anjarlekar, Rasoul Etesami, R Srikant

This router learns individual quality preferences and uses a constraint queue to trade inference cost against satisfaction. Its real-model proof of concept uses 100 queries, with satisfaction outcomes still generated by a simulator.
Tool Recommendation for Multi-Step Agents: Finding Every Tool a Task Needs
Sam Partee, River Stevens, Thierry Damiba, Valerie Fanelle

This deployed system retrieves tools before an agent calls them. On ToolRet, its top ten results contain every required tool 57% more often than BM25, targeting the missing-tool failures that break multi-step workflows.
QD-Rec: Open-Ended Evolution of Recommendations via Quality-Diversity
Takashi Ishida, Taro Makino, Issa Sugiura

QD-Rec searches over item–rationale pairs, retaining pairs that are novel or better than nearby archived alternatives. Experiments span four task families: acquisitions, customer targeting, papers, and books.
EKLAV: Elicited Key CoT Learning via Answer only superVision
Adarsh Singh, Aman Singh, Kushal Raj Bhandari, Soham Dan, Anoop Kumar, Vivek Gupta
EKLAV provides teacher reasoning as training context while supervising only answers. It wins 41 of 48 model-domain comparisons on BRIGHT reranking.
Jev-as-a-Judge for Brazilian Portuguese Information Retrieval: Relevance Assessment and Reranking
Jev supplies relevance labels and reranks Portuguese search results. On Quati, nDCG@10 rises from 0.3329 to 0.6331 over BM25.
Steering beyond Language: Improving Multilingual Training-Free Text Embeddings via Paired-Residual Subspace Removal
Ailiang Lin, Zhuoyun Li, Yusong Wang, Keyu Mao, Kotaro Funakoshi, Manabu Okumura
PRSR removes language-specific directions estimated from parallel sentences, without training the underlying LLM. Monolingual evaluation spans 18 languages.
Evidence-Gated Bilingual RAG for Reliable Consumer Banking Search
Ahmed Mohamed Mahmoud Rayyan, Rana Mahmoud Mohammed, Aya Abdallah Abdelmonem, Mohamed Khaled Goda O…
A local bilingual banking search pipeline combines hybrid retrieval, reranking and evidence-based answer gating. Top-1 hit rate rises from 50.48% to 79.05% on 210 queries.
Code Skill Server: A Large-Scale Search Engine for Code Generation Skills
Xiaoyong Li, Haolong Li, Dongliang Xu, Haoyu Li, Yifan Wang, Jingyuan Shi, Yanghua Wang, Yanbin Sun…
Code Skill Server indexes 993 reusable coding skills and evaluates their retrieval through downstream code generation. The best configuration improves Pass@1 by up to 13.91%.
ReaLiC: Reward-aligned latent reasoning for conversational query rewriting
Liang Xu, Guanyu Qin, Zibo Yi, Yunbo Cao, Zhunchen Luo, Lei Shi, Feifei Kou

ReaLiC trains explicit rewriting strategies with rewards for retrieval effectiveness and contextual consistency. It evaluates two conversational retrieval benchmarks; the accessible preview does not expose numerical gains.
SAG2: Embedding-Free Multi-Hop Retrieval with BM25 and JEV
SAG2 combines SQLite, BM25 and query-time evidence decisions for multi-hop retrieval. Recall@10 reaches 86.62% on a 1,000-question MuSiQue subset.
Gap Detection: Mitigating Homogenization through Demand and Defensibility
Xucheng Yu, Haibo Jin, Xiaoqi Wang, Runze Kong, Haohan Wang
Gap Detection searches embedding space for relevant but uncovered directions. Across five curated topics, mean relative output-collision reduction is 12.8%.
Inside Prometheus: Meta’s Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster

Meta describes power, cooling and capacity planning for its Prometheus training cluster, with a roadmap toward roughly one million GPUs. This is an infrastructure target, not a measured search-quality gain.
Acceptance Is Not Speed: Length Inflation in Training-Free Lossy Speculative Decoding
Chiatzen Wang, Bill Xu, Haochen Gu, Hongyang Zhang

Relaxed speculative verification can inflate completions enough to erase apparent decoding gains. Across matched prompts, the study tracks completion length, verifier rounds, runtime and accuracy. At the most relaxed settings, accepted tokens per round rise 1.34× while completions grow 1.54×.
Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short-Answer F1 Loss

Reducing experts during prompt processing saves compute, but a few prompt positions account for much of the quality loss. Token-level interventions favor preserving full expert computation near task interfaces over random document positions. Time to first token falls about 14% on long prompts.
DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
Jiaming Xu, Hanzhen Wang, Tianlang Zhao, Jiewen Xiao, Chengze Yuan, Jiayi Pan, Yongkang Zhou, Jianc…

DLite removes explicit historical context from the speculative drafter by reusing contextual hidden states from the target model. A lightweight sequential head restores dependencies within each proposed block. The paper reports improvements of up to 70% over DSpark.
Accelerated Dataflow: scaling inference in streaming data analytics with efficiency
RuiLong Jiang, Dustin Rhodes, Danny McCormick, Yuta Labur, Reza Rokni

Accelerated Dataflow coordinates autoscaling across heterogeneous worker pools with prefix-aware batching for streaming LLM pipelines. It addresses inference-heavy workloads that conventional streaming engines handle poorly. Reported throughput improves 1.5–2× at similar latency.
Reusing Calibration Gains across Model Representations

This study transfers group-wise calibration gains between representations of the same pretrained model without optimizing the recipient. Quantized integer codes and storage layout stay fixed. On the tested Qwen3 pair, transfer retains 76.9–90.5% of recipient-specific text-loss gains.
Simplify AI search with AlloyDB hybrid search and RRF

AlloyDB combines vector and full-text retrieval through a native SQL interface with reciprocal rank fusion, avoiding application-side score normalization and joins. It also supports additional text indexes and external search sources. The example uses one declarative SQL call; this is an integration result, not a throughput multiplier.
HydraLLM: Adaptive Width Slicing for Elastic Text and Vision-Language Models
Oscar Kemme, Janek Haberer, Ali Hojjat, Olaf Landsiedel

HydraLLM converts a pretrained checkpoint into nested subnetworks whose embedding, attention, feed-forward and output widths follow the active head count. Weight reordering and distillation train the elastic family. At one-quarter of the heads, token-generation throughput rises 75.3% over full width.
SP$^2$ec: Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
Yuqi Huang, Xingyao Li, Yunlong Hou, Fengzhuo Zhang, Jiachun Pan, Vincent Y. F. Tan

SP²ec adapts self-speculative draft configurations during generation rather than fixing one for every multimodal prompt. Its bandit algorithm exploits an observed single-peaked throughput curve and accounts for exploration time. Tested visual and text workloads improve by up to 11% over the underlying methods.
Peak-Memory Schedules You Can Trust: Exact Realization, Certified Optimality, and the Limits of Recomputation for Inference
Ivan Fomin, Ivan Koryabkin, Boris Sheludko

This work reorders statements in the compiled program rather than recompiling a reordered graph, which can miss its predicted memory peak. Read/write modeling supports exact accounting under stated allocation conditions. Lower bounds certify optimal schedules for 94% of held-out wrapper graphs.
CascadeLedger: Counterfactual Auditing of Information and Resource Integrity in LLM Cascades
Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Daren Zha

CascadeLedger audits whether a budgeted LLM cascade used only information legally available at each decision. It records calls, cache identities and budget transitions, then applies counterfactual checks to frozen traces. The reported detection rate for serialized faults is 99.83%.
Grounded Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Search Agents
Qirui Liu, Hao Chen, Yi Wen, Weijie Shi, Yao Zhao, Xianhe Chen, Hao Zhao, Xing Tang, Weihong Luo, Y…

A search agent can answer correctly without using retrieved evidence. Grounded Credit Assignment separates credit for finding evidence from credit for answering. On the larger evaluated model, it improves average exact match over Search-R1 by 6.3 percentage points.
MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups
Markus Fischer, Jens Meiler, Matthias Elgeti

Munin indexes a local literature corpus and citation graph, then equips an open-weight model with reading, search, and computation tools. On paired literature questions, accuracy rises from 38.7% without the harness to 87.4% with it.
When Does Uncertainty Measure RAG Hallucination Risk?

Model confidence tracks unsupported answers only when retrieved evidence constrains the response. Across controlled unsupported edits, perplexity achieves AUROC between 0.81 and 0.91 after answer-length matching.
GLOBE: Evolving Structured Agentic Memory for E-commerce Product Optimization in Generative Search
Hyunseo Kim, Suil Choe, Sukkyoung So, Daeyeon Yi

GLOBE stores product-editing experience as explicit rules scoped to listing fields. Feedback updates the handbook, while moderation removes redundancy and deactivates harmful rules. Ranking-improvement success rises by 17.5 percentage points over prompt optimization.
SAFE-Mem: Secure Agentic Memory with Fine-Grained Authority and Governance-Aware Retrieval
Haoming Li, Dingyi Kang, Xu Hu, Jinxin Yang, Zhu Xu, Chenru Wang, Yi Ge, Miao Yin, Guanpeng Li, Fen…

SAFE-Mem labels individual memory claims by kind, authority, and scope, then checks those permissions during retrieval. Attack success is at least 77% lower than the strongest evaluated defense that preserves legitimate memory use.
Explore Separately, Adopt Selectively: Execution-Guided Tool Use over Large Tool Libraries
Anna Mazhar, Seiji Maekawa, Nikita Bhutani
BRIA tests candidate tools in isolated branches and lets the task agent adopt only useful execution evidence. On MCP-Atlas, its average claim score exceeds MCP-Zero by 14.37 percentage points.
Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
Heming Zou, Qi Wang, Yixiu Mao, Yun Qu, Yuyi Guo, Zeyuan Liu, Chenglin Li, Weijie Liu, Saiyong Yang…

TreeOPSD branches continuations from shared interaction prefixes, backs terminal rewards up the tree, and distills toward a bounded teacher distribution. It improves average Deep Research accuracy over GRPO by 4.97 percentage points on the reported model.
MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
Yuhan Sun, Jiaxin Zhao, Yongdong Luo, Yibo Hu, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma, Weixun Wang, Weihang Pan,…

MultiAgent-OPD trains a Leader–Searcher–Answerer team with role-specific feedback and token-level supervision from a frozen teacher. Across seven datasets, macro avg@4 exceeds Prompted Critic by 4.06 percentage points.
Understanding KV Residency in Production-Scale Agentic LLM Workloads
Mayank Arya, Agrim Bari, Anjaly Parayil, Yogesh Simmhan, Renee St. Amant, Victor R\"uhle, Saravan R…

A study of production agent workloads examines how long KV state occupies GPU memory between model calls. Trace-driven replay with a public KV layout finds that a one-hour idle cap reduces the estimated residency ceiling by 3.6 times.
Build observable enterprise agentic retrieval using Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with AWS CloudFormation

AWS provides a deployable reference for iterative retrieval across managed knowledge bases, an MCP gateway, and an instrumented agent runtime. Seven telemetry layers cover retrieval, traces, token usage, and evaluation. The post reports no comparative answer-quality uplift.
Gryphon-v2: One Model in Place of a Cascade - Generate-and-Rank Recommender with Rollout Distillation
Lipkina, Anna, Tikhonovich, Daria, Yanush, Viktor, Ulianova, Mariia, Sorokin, Oleg, Dodonov, Vladis…

Gryphon-v2 encodes user history once, generates semantic item IDs, and ranks the resolved items with a small shared-state head. A larger teacher supplies training targets but stays out of serving. Replacing the Yandex Music cascade increased active users by 1.41% in an online experiment.
Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence
Xiao, Yang, Sun, Yusong, Wu, Haoyi, Hui, Wenyang, Hang, Weiqiang, Wang, Luqing, Wang, Zejian, Tu, Z…

Vela turns real behavior histories into tasks and accepted training trajectories rather than treating logs only as next-click labels. Fine-tuning on this supervision improves user-related tasks by up to 11.5 points over the base model.
When Machines Speak: A Unified Generative Framework for Integrating Machine-Native Symbols into Pretrained Large Language Models

UniLang adds grounded machine-native symbols to a pretrained LLM vocabulary so text and item codes share one autoregressive objective. On MovieLens-20M, its reported NDCG@5 improvement over the strongest tabulated baseline is about 151.7%.
LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising
Zhang, Wen, Bai, Xiao, Chao, Hsiang-wei, Zhu, Mengfan, Zhao, Tong, Ju, Mingxuan, Liu, Xiaodong, Zha…

This DPA evaluation method compresses behavior into intent representatives and uses an LLM judge, later distilled into a student, to score user-product relevance. One evaluated content retrieval strategy achieved a 4.98% online CVR increase; that is a strategy result, not a causal gain from the judge.
PsyBer-Agent: A Psychology-Driven User Agent for Recommender Systems
Zhang, Chong, Shen, Qijie, Zhang, Haichao, Wang, Can, Jin, Xiaobo, Wang, Jia

PsyBer-Agent simulates evolving user states and calibrates its trajectories against interaction logs. A lightweight policy handles most decisions, with occasional LLM fallback. Its five-million queued-task test reports a 95.18% success rate.
When More Data Is Not Enough: The Context-Sufficiency Frontier in Generative AI Personalization

A retail experiment tests combinations of relevant and irrelevant provider context. For one customer, held-out recommendation appropriateness falls from 0.94 with a smaller context set to 0.88 with all signals. Extra context can disrupt retrieval even when the model does not adopt it.
Learning When to Think: Utility-Guided Adaptive Reasoning for Efficient Text Retrieval
Luo, Yingtao, Zhao, Kangyi, Du, Shiyi, Li, Yubo

AURA supervises intermediate reasoning by how well embeddings separate relevant documents from hard negatives. A small utility estimator selects the stopping point. Under matched deployment conditions, adaptive stopping reduces latency from 4.6 to 0.76 seconds versus full-trajectory reasoning.
How Can Recommendation Feedback Evolve Agent Memory?
Mao, Shanwen, Li, Mingming, Zhang, Hao, Li, Zhiheng, Wang, Yige, Yu, Penghua, Zhu, Junxiong

TIDE attributes delayed recommendation feedback to the memories used by a content-generation agent, then reinforces, modifies, or evicts those memories. In offline temporal replay for e-commerce marketing, it reports a 7.75-percentage-point Memory Evolution Gain.
LIFT: A Lifecycle-aware Interaction Factorization Transformer for Unified Retrieval and Ranking
Miao, Keji, Cheng, Enhao, Li, Yan, Li, Qun, Zhang, Qi, Yuan, Jie, Li, Xiaoyong

LIFT factorizes an interaction into Request, Item, Context, and Action states in causal order. Retrieval and ranking read different states from one shared history model. Its Joint Score improves by 3.6% over the strongest evaluated baseline on Taobao.
Aligning LLMs with Sparse Retrieval via Adaptive Sparse Supervision
Chen, Tongna, Li, Minghan, Zhou, Guodong

Input-adaptive sparse supervision trains an LLM retriever to retain salient lexical activations without a fixed support budget. Compared with Lion-sp, the paper reports 6.4-fold smaller index storage and competitive retrieval effectiveness.
TransX Technical Report: Scaling Sequence Transduction for Recommendation
Xu, Da, Fang, Liyan, Venugopalan, Divya, Hsu, Sunny, Wang, Xukai, Chowdhury, Rishav Roy, Liang, Cin…

TransX caches reusable behavior memory and separates sequence encoding from candidate-conditioned scoring. Offline prefill and nearline refresh keep history processing off the request path. Its base model raised CTR by 6.02% over the production baseline in an online experiment.
RecSoup: Efficient Model Merging Approach for Controllable Multi-Objective Recommendation
Jia, Zidong, Xie, Guofu, Zhang, Xiao

RecSoup makes accuracy–diversity trade-offs adjustable by reusing objective-specific checkpoints. It prunes task-vector updates and learns preference-dependent merge coefficients. Parameter construction was about 165–228 times faster than a hypernetwork across three benchmarks.
Agentic-Priors: Using Large Language Models to Address the Cold Start Problem in Preference Elicitation
Arcanjo, Bruno, Li, Zhaoxing, Stein, Sebastian

Agentic-Priors asks a language model for interpretable trade-offs, maps them to priors over choice-model coefficients and updates them with observed choices. Across seven datasets, cold-start accuracy exceeded an uninformed prior by 5–40 percentage points.
Understanding and Mitigating Training Instability in Large-Scale Recommender Systems: A Cascade Perspective
Li, Yuening, Wang, Zeyu, Zhang, Zhen, Liu, Jiayi, Jiang, Zhimeng, Roh, Yuji, Xu, Weikai, Gao, Mingy…

Google studies training divergence as a gradient–weight–loss cascade and maps interventions to each stage. The combined treatment improved AUC by 0.38% relative to baseline on the second binary classification task.
Hybrid transformer-based recommender system with LLM-assisted semantic modeling for sequential and federated learning

LLMTransRec combines item identity, genre metadata and BERT-derived text representations in a Transformer for next-item prediction. It reports offline tests on four benchmarks; the federated component is a feasibility study. The accessible page does not quantify the main gains.
CalendarRec: Multi-Order Temporal Context for Sequential Recommendation
CalendarRec adds separate month, day and weekday representations to a Mamba-based sequential recommender. On health-functional-food click logs, NDCG@10 improved by 14.2% relative to Mamba4Rec.
Encoded but Exposed: Language Embeddings can Reveal More Than They Should in Recommender Systems

Language embeddings can expose item identities through similarity matching against public descriptions. Experiments on two datasets also show that item leakage can enable user re-identification from sparse ratings. Obfuscation reduces leakage but harms recommendation utility.
Reliability-aware ensemble recommendation for open-network commerce: a dual-metric framework for jointly evaluating ranking accuracy and serving correctness

This study separates ranking quality from serving correctness in open-network commerce. In controlled trace replays, routing and identifier fixes raised route resolution success from 60.0% to 99.8%. These are reproducible system experiments, not production A/B results.
MARS: A Momentum-Aware Adaptive Rating System for Personalized Assessment
Sahu, Vikrant, Naik, Khethavath Sunil, Gupta, Gagan Raj

MARS combines a question knowledge graph with momentum-sensitive proficiency updates and time-budgeted routing. In its negative-marking experiment, overtime violations fell from 50% to 5.6%. The evaluation concerns adaptive assessment rather than media recommendation.
Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents
Chenxi Li , Xueyang Feng , Songyang Liu , Chenxu Wang , Xiaoying Tang , Chaozhuo Li , Litian Zhang

The method calibrates on-policy distillation with information gained after retrieval, adjusting both turn-level supervision and query preferences. The 2B student gains 3.4 accuracy points on average across six multimodal search benchmarks.
Retrieved but Not Read: Understanding Why Search-Augmented LLMs Fail to Use Available Evidence
Owen Walters , Lihu Chen , Francesca Toni

The study separates finding current evidence from using it in the final answer. Across six open-weight configurations and a proprietary deployment, models sometimes rely on snippets and retain stale answers despite available evidence.
TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents
Tanish Kher , Sarvesh DK , Abedelkadir Asi , Sparsha Chennarayapatna Sundaresh , Dezhi Hong

TRACER indexes observed tool-call sequences in a trie and combines empirical and contextual priors to rank continuations. In a mixed retail and telecom setting, tool-selection accuracy improves by 4.7 points.
SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems
Giancarlo Maldonado Cárdenas , Carlos A. Astudillo , Nelson L. S. da Fonseca

SSR uses structural lexical signals from Agent Cards and an inverted index to preselect agents without training. At 1,000 agents, orchestration latency falls by 70.9% relative to passing the complete catalog.
GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models
Weiting Liu , Zhiyu Pan , Shuhong Wang , Zhenquan Yao , Jungang Li , Li Zhao , Jian Jiang , Jianfen…

GACC-Bench tests whether compressed context preserves information for a goal before the exact questions are known. It contains 500 goals. Goal conditioning helps, but even the best tested compressor falls short of full context.
CARA: Causally Guided Retrieval Agent for Question Answering
Weicheng Liu , Xiangcheng Wu , Depeng Xu , Haopeng Zhang , Xi Niu

CARA evaluates evidence through addition and removal tests, then combines these signals with path consistency for graph exploration. It is tested on three STaRK datasets; the abstract does not give a single aggregate improvement.
Push-Based KV Transfer to Improve TTFT and TPOT for Disaggregated Inference in vLLM

A push-based NIXL connector overlaps destination allocation with prefill and moves transfer setup off the decode loop. In the specified Qwen3-32B 1P1D test on EC2 P5en with EFA, TTFT improves by up to about 3× over pull mode.
Improve TTFT for Multi-Turn Agentic Workloads with Bi-Directional KV Transfer in vLLM
Bidirectional KV transfer lets prefill nodes reuse state produced on decode nodes in earlier turns. In the specified GLM-5-FP8 1P1D multi-turn benchmark, TTFT improves by up to 3.3×.
Adaptive Verification Without a Confidence Head
